messages:
ash: Heads-up — we're seeing a spike of tiny-pod evictions in ap-southeast1 over the last 40m. Likely related to attach failures on warm nodes.

ash: Quick metrics snapshot:
```
attach_failures{zone="apse1"} 324 -> 1,120 (1h)
gpu_pod_evictions_total{reason="preemptive"} 87 -> 342
warmpool_unbinds 12 -> 78
median_pod_gpu_request 0.125 -> 0.0625
```

maria: Ugh. Is this the conntrack/egress thing again or NIC flaps?

ash: Logs show a bunch of `attach timeout` + `device not found` while kubelet retries. Some racks report intermittent fabric errors. Not classic conntrack but similar attach latency.

jin: Any correlation with recent node kernel updates or the rack NIC firmware rollout? I pushed a small firmware patch to two racks ~2h ago.

leo: FYI cost note — when small pods fail to attach they fallback to larger reserved instances in other zones, so we saw cross-az fallbacks and a ~18% uplift in tokenized GPU-hours for affected customers.

maria: Can we isolate whether scheduler is causing fragmentation? If tiny-pods keep getting descheduled we end up with many 0.125 GPU holes. Need to check binpacking heuristics + anti-affinity behavior.

ash: Agree. Heatmap shows many tiny holes on shelf nodes, and scheduler keep placing 0.125-GPU pods which leaves 0.0625 leftover slots that can't fit typical tiny-gangs.

leo: Proposed mitigations:
- increase warmpool size in apse1 by +25% for next 2h
- temporarily bias scheduler to prefer compact packing (reduce spread score by 30%)
- enable a short defrag drain job for nodes with <0.1 GPU free (canary 2 nodes)

maria: i'm +1 on warmpool bump and compact bias asap. Defrag drain needs ops guardrails — we should avoid mass preempts during business hours.

jin: I'll roll back the firmware patch on the two racks and watch attach failures for 15m. If it reduces, we can mark that patch as suspect.

ops-bot: deploy:warmpool-adjustment started by leo (canary) — increasing apse1 warmpool target by 25% (2 nodes).

ash: After the warmpool bump, attach failures dropped to ~420 in 10m window (was 1,120). Evictions reduced by ~45%. Looks promising but still elevated.

maria: Scheduler-side change: I'll open a canary to lower spread scoring on compact-scheduler for apse1 only. Will monitor fragmentation heatmap and eviction rates.

jin: Firmware rollback seemed to help on the two racks I rolled back — attach timeouts down to baseline there. I'll escalate to infra to pause that rollout.

leo: Cost note: If compaction reduces cross-az fallbacks we'll save ~12% on short-term spillover costs. Keep monitoring.

ash: TL;DR: suspected NIC/firmware rollout + attach latency caused warmpool churn -> tiny-pod evictions -> fragmentation. Actions: rollback firmware rollout (jin), warmpool bump (leo), scheduler compaction canary (maria), small defrag drain guarded (ops).

maria: I'm going to add a short regression eval to Redwood Optimize to watch output quality from compact placement — want to ensure we don't regress tail latency.

ash: Thanks team. We'll keep this thread updated with metrics.
